sections.title: Sound of the letter En
paragraphs: The letter is called (En) /ɛn/. Its main sound is in (Name) /ˈnaːmə/, what people call you. This letter makes three sounds.

sections.title: How to say the sounds
paragraphs: For the first sound, press the tip of your tongue against the ridge behind your upper teeth. Let the air go through your nose with your voice on. For the next sound, lift the back of your tongue against the soft roof. Touch your throat to feel it shake. For the last sound, hold that nose air to make a whole beat.

sections.title: When to use each sound
paragraphs: You hear the main sound in most positions, as in (nein) /naɪ̯n/. Before k or g, the back of your mouth takes over, as in (danke) /ˈdaŋkə/. In unstressed endings, the letter can form its own beat without any vowel, as in (leben) /ˈleːbn̩/.

sections.title: Mistakes to avoid
paragraphs: Do not drop the final nose beat when you say words like (laufen) /ˈlaʊ̯fn̩/. Keep your voice going and let the air escape through your nose without adding a full vowel. Always lift the back of your tongue smoothly before a k sound, just like in the English word sink.
